sources: National Center for O*NET Development - Data Entry Keyers (Standard Occupational Classification 43-9021.00)
AHIMA (American Health Information Management Association) Data Quality and Integrity Guidelines
rules: Raw input strings and alphanumeric records must match source documents with zero tolerance for undetected transcription errors.
Corrupted, ambiguous, or gibberish input strings must be flagged and routed to exception quarantine rather than blindly committed.
Data throughput must maintain a minimum target of 60 Net Words Per Minute (WPM) or 10,000 Keystrokes Per Hour (KPH) at 99.8% accuracy.
assumptions: The operator uses an ergonomic mechanical QWERTY keyboard with standard 10-key numeric pad.
Input documents include mixed alphanumeric strings, dirty scans, and distorted OCR output requiring manual sanitization.
The target terminal runs a validated relational database entry form with real-time field validation hooks.

levels.title: Alphanumeric Transcription & Noise Filtering
levels.goal: Accurately transcribe raw, noisy alphanumeric strings and identify unverified character artifacts with 100% precision.
levels.description: Operators master high-speed transcription of non-dictionary alphanumeric strings and identify unintentional keystrokes or noise bursts before committing records.
customerProfiles: Records supervisor auditing raw catalog intake batches where misspelled identifiers break downstream lookups.
successConditions: Transcribe all 15 alphanumeric batches with >= 99.8% character accuracy
Zero unflagged garbage strings committed to the main index
Average entry pace of >= 8,000 keystrokes per hour
steps: Position hands on home row (A-S-D-F / J-K-L-;) and align source sheet in document clip
Transcribe string token character by character without glancing at keyboard
Compare entered token against source string using terminal hash verification
Flag corrupted tokens (e.g. non-ASCII artifacts or random keyboard mash) using shortcut Alt+Q
Submit validated batch and verify terminal confirms zero validation warnings
checks: All flagged exceptions logged with exact line number and timestamp

levels.title: OCR Exception Handling & String Normalization
levels.goal: Reconcile degraded optical character recognition (OCR) output against source scans, correcting character confusion errors within 45 seconds per record.
levels.description: Scanned documents often yield OCR errors where '0' becomes 'O', '1' becomes 'l', or random keystrokes appear. Operators must normalize strings into standard formatting.
customerProfiles: Inventory control manager requiring cleaned SKU references for automated warehouse picking.
successConditions: Correct 100% of alphanumeric substitution errors across 20 manifests
Zero regex pattern mismatches on final SKU strings
Processing time under 45 seconds per manifest record
steps: Split terminal view: digital scan on left display, OCR buffer on right display
Scan string for common substitution pitfalls (0 vs O, 1 vs I/l, 5 vs S, 8 vs B)
Replace corrupted characters with validated glyphs from source scan
Execute automated regex check (Format: ^[A-Z]{3}-[0-9]{5}-[A-Z0-9]$) via Ctrl+Enter
Commit record and move immediately to next manifest in queue
checks: Total cycle time for 20 manifests <= 15 minutes
Zero rejected records upon database ingest

levels.title: Blind Double-Entry Verification & Collision Resolution
levels.goal: Execute blind re-keying on high-consequence transaction fields and resolve discrepancy collisions under strict SLA timers.
levels.description: Financial and medical databases require blind secondary entry where the operator re-keys critical fields without seeing the primary operator's values. Any mismatch triggers an immediate collision review.
customerProfiles: Compliance auditor enforcing SOX (Sarbanes-Oxley) segregation and dual-entry integrity standards.
successConditions: Complete 30 blind verification records with zero undetected character collisions
Resolve all detected discrepancies with 100% alignment to original source proof
Sustain entry speed >= 10,000 keystrokes per hour
steps: Open blind record buffer; primary values remain masked in the database backend
Key in secondary alphanumeric identifier and monetary value using 10-key numeric pad
Press Tab to advance and trigger backend checksum differential comparison
If collision warning sounds, review source scan proof at 200% magnification to confirm truth
Select definitive character value, input reason code 'SRC_VERIFIED', and stamp record
checks: Backend discrepancy collision rate resolves to 0 unresolved items
Audit trail contains operator signature and timestamp on every corrected entry
Gross entry speed meets or exceeds 10,000 KPH

levels.title: High-Velocity Batch Ingestion & Integrity Audit
levels.goal: Process a backlog of 50 multi-field entries under simulated shift pressure with zero database rollbacks and under 1.5% total exception overhead.
levels.description: Operators handle high-throughput queue conditions combining raw typing, exception routing, format normalization, and batch reconciliation against master totals.
customerProfiles: Operations director requiring end-of-day batch closeout without reconciliation discrepancies or overtime.
successConditions: Batch balance checksum matches master ledger hash exactly (delta = 0)
Quarantine exception rate <= 1.5% of total records processed
steps: Initialize batch session and log beginning ledger control checksum
Transcribe header, line-item identifiers, and transactional amounts without pause
Perform rapid in-line triage on ambiguous strings: fix known corruptions or route to quarantine within 5 seconds
Run batch total checksum comparison against pre-calculated control slip
Investigate any balancing delta down to the individual line item until variance equals 0.00
Sign off batch manifest and transmit clean ledger to master database
checks: Zero uncommitted records left in local memory buffer
All quarantined items accompanied by standardized incident metadata
